skill.name: software-testing-router
skill.description: Choose appropriate test interfaces for CLI, API, web, Qt, and native desktop workflows using scoped automation and verifiable results.
skill.summary: Route software tests to suitable interfaces and verify outcomes with scoped actions, bounded waits, and durable evidence.
skill.author: hunxuankai

security_audit.summary: All 147 static findings are false positives after contextual review of documentation, evidence files, and process-scoped automation code. Subprocesses launch packaged workers without shell interpolation; URLs are research citations, while entropy flags reflect readable Chinese text and serialized JUnit XML. No evidence found of credential theft, unauthorized exfiltration, or prompt injection; desktop actions still require authorized targets and platform permissions.

content.value_statement: Software tests can use unsuitable interfaces and produce incomplete evidence. This skill selects suitable testing routes and provides scoped desktop helpers with explicit verification boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Select CLI, API, DOM, UIA, AX, Qt, or visual checks according to the behavior requiring proof.
Inspect Windows controls and execute scoped set, invoke, and wait steps with unique selectors and process identity checks.
Provide a macOS AX implementation with PID binding, exact selectors, permission checks, and protected password controls.
Preserve desktop progress in local journals and distinguish completed steps from actions with unknown outcomes after interruption.
Guide web tests through scoped DOM locators, real button events, response checks, and independent output verification.
Document Qt signal testing, cancellation assertions, controlled image comparisons, and historical validation boundaries.
limitations: The macOS native implementation has no real Mac validation evidence for Intel or Apple Silicon.
Windows automation requires Windows, Python 3.10 or newer, PowerShell 7, and an interactive desktop; Linux has no packaged native driver.
Packaged desktop helpers support set, invoke, and wait only; they do not provide global keyboard, mouse, or coordinate fallback.
The runtime package excludes maintenance tests and fixtures; historical results do not establish universal compatibility or speed improvements.

use_cases.title: Validate a Source-Free Windows Application
use_cases.description: Inspect a known EXE, scope duplicate controls, run an export flow, and verify the newly generated file independently.

use_cases.title: Verify an Asynchronous Web Form
use_cases.description: Choose scoped DOM automation and connect a real submit event to its response, business status, and resulting artifact.

use_cases.title: Plan Cross-Interface Release Checks
use_cases.description: Separate API, internal Qt, packaged application, and visual assertions while identifying missing platform evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starting Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [application] and [expected behavior]. Identify available test interfaces, select a suitable route, and state the evidence required.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: identify a suitable testing interface before writing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Web Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: For [URL], inspect the export dialog and its duplicate controls. Plan a real button interaction, bounded waits, and independent output verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: verify a web event and its business result.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Scoped Desktop Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: For authorized [PID], [executable], and [window], inspect controls first. Build unique set, invoke, and wait steps with bounded execution and new evidence files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: automate an identified desktop application without global input.

prompt_templates.title: Assess an Interrupted Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [journal], [report], and current application state without replaying actions. Identify completed steps, unknown outcomes, missing evidence, and a justified next step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess possible side effects after a worker timeout.

output_examples.input: Choose checks for a file converter with an official CLI and no interface acceptance requirement.
output: Selected route: official CLI using separate process arguments and a finite timeout.
Required evidence: successful exit, expected business result, and independently checked content from a fresh output file.
Boundary: this verifies conversion, not desktop buttons or visual appearance.

output_examples.input: A Windows export action timed out after it started. Determine whether it should run again.
output: Outcome: unknown because the journal records action start without confirmed completion.
Next step: inspect current application state and the current run's output before considering another action.
Boundary: terminating the automation worker does not undo effects in the target application.

output_examples.input: Assess whether the packaged Mac helper is ready for release acceptance.
output: Implementation available: process-scoped AX inspection and set, invoke, and wait steps.
Missing evidence: real Mac execution, native ABI compatibility, permission ownership, and actual target control behavior.
Conclusion: plan authorized native validation; do not report simulated or skipped checks as passing.

best_practices: Inspect actual interfaces and control capabilities before selecting tools or writing selectors.
Use fresh test data and independent business assertions rather than treating action dispatch or file existence as success.
Set bounded waits and worker deadlines, then inspect journals and target state before retrying interrupted actions.
anti_patterns: Replacing a required button interaction with a direct API call and claiming the interface passed.
Using first matches, guessed coordinates, broader process scopes, or automatic elevation to bypass missing capabilities.
Treating skipped tests, simulated platform checks, or historical sample timings as universal validation.

faq.question: Does this skill always require Computer Use?
faq.answer: No. It prioritizes suitable structured interfaces and treats visual interaction as a constrained fallback when permitted.

faq.question: Can it test a Windows application without source code?
faq.answer: Yes, when the application exposes suitable UIA controls and patterns. The helper verifies the supplied executable, PID, and process start time.

faq.question: Is the macOS helper verified on real hardware?
faq.answer: No. The implementation exists, but real Mac ABI, permissions, and GUI behavior remain unverified.

faq.question: Does it provide native Linux desktop automation?
faq.answer: No. The portable entry point reports native desktop automation as unavailable on Linux. Other testing routes depend on the target environment.

faq.question: Does a completed invoke step prove business success?
faq.answer: No. It proves action dispatch only. Verify the expected application state and current run's artifacts independently.

faq.question: Are all referenced tests included in the installed package?
faq.answer: No. The runtime package contains helpers, references, and historical evidence. Maintenance tests, fixtures, and development dependencies remain in the source repository.
